How to use this calculator

  1. Enter body weight, standard drinks, hours since drinking began and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How bac is calculated

Estimated BAC% ≈ alcohol grams ÷ (r×body weight grams) × 100 − 0.015×hours, floored at zero. Absorption, drink size, food, and metabolism vary widely. A modelled estimate can change substantially if drink strength, body composition, or timing differs from the inputs.

Widmark-style estimate: ethanol/(r×body mass)×100−0.015×hours.
A worked example

A modelled estimate can change substantially if drink strength, body composition, or timing differs from the inputs.

Assumptions & useful context

Highly uncertain educational estimate; never use it to decide whether to drive, cycle, or operate equipment.

Health calculations are estimates for education. They cannot diagnose a condition or replace a clinician’s assessment. Individual needs vary, especially during pregnancy, illness and growth.

Frequently asked questions

Can this tell me if I am safe to drive?

No. Do not use a calculator to make that decision.

Is the estimate a measured BAC?

No. Only a suitable test can measure alcohol concentration.
